title: Student Movement Wins Big Election in Serbia
summary:
Big election news came from Serbia this weekend. Serbia is a small country in southeastern Europe with under seven million people. Its longtime leader, Aleksandar Vucic, lost a historic election on Sunday, and his government fell.

What makes this win special, experts say, is who led it: students. The movement had no single leader. It was spread out, not run from the top, and it used online tools to organize.

The protesters' main focus was corruption in government. Vucic had once served in the cabinet of Slobodan Milosevic, a former Serbian leader. The win follows a recent election in Hungary that also fought corruption, and it is seen as a setback for Russia and China.

This was not a race against one rival. In a parliamentary election, voters choose parties, not a single president. When polls showed his party losing badly, Vucic admitted defeat peacefully, which surprised observers.

The big question now is what comes next. If the student-led movement cannot form a government, Vucic's side could fight another day.
